source.section: Form N-11 lines 7-12, 19-20 and 23-27 (pages 2-3); PDF page 11 (Line 7), PDF page 20 (Line 23 standard deduction table, Line 25 exemptions), PDF page 9 (Lines 6a, 6b, 'age 65 or over as of January 1, 2026'), PDF page 20 (Line 27 Tax Table), PDF page 50 (2025 Tax Rate Schedules)

worked: Single, 45, wages 60,000. No Hawaii additions or subtractions. Line 7 federal AGI = wages 60,000.00 = 60,000.00. Federal taxable income = 60,000.00 - 15,750.00 federal standard deduction = 44,250.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Line 11 total additions = 0.00; line 12 = 60,000.00 + 0.00 = 60,000.00. Line 19 total subtractions = 0.00; line 20 Hawaii AGI = 60,000.00 - 0.00 = 60,000.00. Line 23 standard deduction (single, PDF page 20 table) 4,400.00; line 24 = 60,000.00 - 4,400.00 = 55,600.00. Line 6e exemptions: 1 regular = 1; line 25 = 1 x 1,144.00 = 1,144.00. Line 26 taxable income = 55,600.00 - 1,144.00 = 54,456.00. Line 27 tax, Schedule I (PDF page 50) as bands on 54,456.00: 9,600.00 x 1.4% = 134.40; 4,800.00 x 3.2% = 153.60; 4,800.00 x 5.5% = 264.00; 4,800.00 x 6.4% = 307.20; 12,000.00 x 6.8% = 816.00; 12,000.00 x 7.2% = 864.00; 6,456.00 x 7.6% = 490.656; sum = 3,029.856, to the cent 3,029.86; tax = 3,029.86 (Form N-11 line 27 uses the Tax Table below 100,000 of taxable income (PDF page 20, Line 27): the table row 54,450 to 54,500 gives 3,031; this case uses the bands as numbers). No credits modelled (refundable food/excise and renters credits, lines 28-29, not claimed): state income tax = 3,029.86.
